source: Puma et al. (2012), Third Grade Follow-up to the Head Start Impact Study: Final Report, OPRE 2012-45, rendered Exhibits 4.9–4.10 (printed pp. 89–90).
scope: Five treatment-on-the-treated estimates only where their corresponding third-grade ITT finding is already published. They are alternate estimands from the same randomized access study, not additional studies or replications.

rows.name: For children entering Head Start at age four, the third-grade ECLS-K Reading IOT impact was +3.34 points (p = .075).
rows.description: This treatment-on-the-treated estimate corresponds to the same cohort’s published +2.23-point ITT reading estimate. It is selected because the access effect was significant at the report’s 10% threshold and is not a separate trial.
rows.unit: ECLS-K Reading-score treatment-on-the-treated impact at third grade, Head Start participation versus no participation; 4-year-old cohort.

rows.name: For children entering Head Start at age four, the third-grade aggressive-behavior IOT impact was -0.34 points (p = .043).
rows.description: Lower scores indicate fewer behavior problems on this parent-reported measure. This is the participation-scaled counterpart of the published -0.23-point ITT result, not an independent effect.
rows.unit: Regression-adjusted parent-reported aggressive-behavior treatment-on-the-treated impact at third grade; 4-year-old cohort; lower is more favorable.

rows.name: For children entering Head Start at age four, the third-grade IOT impact on being in the normal emotional-symptoms category was -0.09 (p = .005).
rows.description: Lower probability of the normal category is unfavorable on this teacher-reported measure. This is the participation-scaled counterpart of the published ITT result and remains reporter-specific.
rows.unit: Regression-adjusted teacher-reported treatment-on-the-treated impact on being in the normal category for emotional symptoms at third grade; 4-year-old cohort; lower is less favorable.

rows.name: For children entering Head Start at age four, the third-grade peer-relations IOT impact was -0.21 points (p = .020).
rows.description: Lower scores indicate worse peer relations on this child-reported measure. This treatment-on-the-treated estimate is the counterpart of the published -0.14-point ITT result, not separate corroboration.
rows.unit: Regression-adjusted child-reported peer-relations treatment-on-the-treated impact at third grade; 4-year-old cohort; lower is less favorable.

rows.name: For children entering Head Start at age three, the third-grade social-skills-and-positive-approaches IOT impact was +0.34 points (p = .025).
rows.description: Higher scores are more favorable on this parent-reported measure. This treatment-on-the-treated estimate is the counterpart of the published +0.24-point ITT result, not a separate study.
rows.unit: Regression-adjusted parent-reported social-skills-and-positive-approaches-to-learning treatment-on-the-treated impact at third grade; 3-year-old cohort; higher is more favorable.
